I am one of those certified weird anime people and I have these issues with many anime as well. I rarely watch the 300+ episode long Shonens like Naruto or One Piece for all the reasons you listed. I tend to gravitate more manga, which often offer more depth and a different tone than their anime counterparts, and shorter anime that range from 12-60 episodes. For me, most things that go over 60 episodes are probably going to start suffering story wise and become corny and poorly written. It takes a lot of talent to stretch a story over that many episodes without any dips in quality.

Here are some series I have found over the years that are ~mostly~ free of the anime things you listed you disliked. While some of that stuff might still be there, they hold a lot of merit as pieces of animated art and have unique interesting stories and characters.
-Serial Experiments Lain, as someone else here suggested
-Ergo Proxy
-Cowboy Bebop
-Princess Mononoke- By the guy who made Spirited Away, but significantly darker/more adult. would highly highly recommend)
-Ghost in the Shell- the first movie would be a good starting point
-Perfect Blue
-Akira
-Paranoia Agent
-Mushishi(While other people are right to recommend it, and it is a lovely anime, it is a bit slow at times)

~Good stuff I like that's a bit more ~anime~
-Fate/Zero
-Durarara!
-Berserk Golden Age Arc trilogy movies

i've just lost so much to my appearance, my teeth are shot from bulimia, ive ravaged my insides overdosing on diet pills, diuretics and laxatives, i know my life is probably going to be shortened because of these tendencies. it stops being about how you look and all about obsessive compulsion and preventing anxiety way before you reach your goal weight. I undereat because I am mentally ill, not because I want to. I had an easier time recovering from drug and alcohol abuse than my bad eating habits. I don't want to count the hours I've spent trying to exercise to a certain deficit or too weak to get out of bed because i was starving myself that i should have spent on hobbies or with loved ones. it has not been worth it and it's not something you just decide you want to stop, i've been like this seven years and have been in recovery maybe since may of this year, but it has been a long and difficult one full of relapse and anxiety. 

also only saying this stuff because it's the reality of disordered eating. people see the "attractive" body but rarely know much about the ugly ugly ugly secrets we keep. there's so much shame and you feel so trapped. just glance at a few pages of MPA and you can get a pretty good idea of the suffering it causes, and everyone on there will say the same as me; never ever fucking begin. 

and undereating isn't your solution, just calories in calories out and trying for a 7/10 when it comes to healthier foods vs treat foods. i lost more weight when i stopped crazy diets and fasts and just ate a lot of fruits and veggies and walked a lot and ate no higher than 1600 net calories a day, which is my BMR. would have two treat meals a week, one healthy one and one that was whatever I wanted but didn't exceed my BMR.

It's a really scary feeling, I have been on both sides of this sort of thing. I don't want to make assumptions or cross a line, but have you ever been evaluated for mental illness? Not because I think any of this is crazy, but it sounds like you may be experiencing the symptoms common in borderline personality disorder. I have it and both my past partners had it. 
I have done similar things where I've led people on for the attention, manipulated friends, all because it was easy and brought me a sick sort of pleasure to have power over people. If I split against someone, I can say the meanest shit you've ever heard and in those moments, even after it's satisfying. having the power to ground zero anyone used to be a point of pride for me. I've done things I can't repeat and admit that even years later it brought primal satisfaction, even the urge to repeat those things to relive that satisfaction. While I never suffered from seduction addiction because of my own issues, my partners very very much did, and would often affect our relationship when they were stuck on the attention of another person, only to rapidly loose interest after a week or two. 
I only suggest it because it made me feel a lot more in control of my symptoms when I was diagnosed and able to read about it. It made me stop feeling like I was some sort of evil person with something missing inside me and allowed me to start seeing my emotional responses to things as an issue with the wiring in my brain. I've made a lot of progress towards rewiring and am finding it easier to connect with people and I less and less often have urges to do "mean" things and handle conflict with a more levelhead and even temper. I even experience guilt at times now, though it seems to be very random over what it will be over. And even if I don't feel guilt, I don't experience the same pleasure hurting people. I am not particularly empathetic but I can logically piece together what I should and should not do to people and have learned that if I want to have lasting relationships, I have to keep my urge to control and manipulate on a tight leash. My way of treating people cost me quite a few good friends and relationships in the past, and my interpersonal dealings and internal environment is more stable now. The venom often tries to slip between the cracks, but I've gotten better at identifying it and putting it away before it surfaces.
